note: Every exhibit below was captured from the GitHub API by `seed-graveyard --refresh` and committed under necropsy/graveyard/fixtures/ at the pinned commit SHA. The wall is api_verified: the offline demo replays those committed captures, so it needs no network and no keys.

entries.curator_note: Fifty-five thousand stars in the first wave of coding agents, then archived when the model vendors shipped the same capability themselves. The repository is not bad; it was absorbed.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: A tool made redundant by the platform it was built on top of.
entries.failure_mode: absorbed into the platform it extended

entries.curator_note: The toolkit that defined reinforcement-learning benchmarks for a decade, archived in favour of a community successor that kept the name. A repo can be replaced by its own children.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: Superseded by an official successor fork rather than by rot.
entries.failure_mode: superseded by its own successor fork

entries.curator_note: Square's event bus for Android, deprecated on the README in favour of another of Square's own libraries. The maintainer did not vanish; the maintainer changed their mind and said so.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: Retired by its own authors in favour of a sibling project.
entries.failure_mode: retired in favour of the author's sibling library

entries.curator_note: The way nearly every Rails app attached files to a record, deprecated with a recommendation to move to the framework's own built-in. Beloved, load-bearing, and now a migration step.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: A load-bearing library deprecated in favour of the framework it plugged into.
entries.failure_mode: replaced by the host framework's built-in

entries.curator_note: The reference implementation of one of the most cited papers in machine learning. It was never meant to be maintained, only to prove the paper out, and it did that and stopped.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: A research artifact that completed its purpose instead of decaying from neglect.
entries.failure_mode: research artifact whose purpose was served

entries.curator_note: Twelve lines that padded strings, and the removal that took down half the npm ecosystem in 2016. It has no tests and never needed them, which is exactly the kind of thing the scorecard has to be able to say kindly.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: Tiny, test-free, and historically load-bearing on the internet.

entries.curator_note: The source of the most-read book about Git, in a dozen languages. Nothing here is rotting: the work was finished, published, and put to rest deliberately.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: A quiet, dignified end after the work shipped.

entries.curator_note: Shopify's own 'store in a box' toolkit for template designers, open-sourced in 2010 and last touched in May 2012. No licence file, no pipeline, no successor, and fourteen years of silence. This is the corpse the scorecard is most certain about.
entries.why_it_is_a_good_exhibit: The deepest real decay on the wall: unlicensed, untested, and silent since 2012.
entries.failure_mode: abandoned with no licence and no successor
